audioScript:
Boy: This is a busy street, isn’t it, Aunt Emma?
Woman: Yes, this is the village where I live.
Boy: Can you see the woman who’s wearing that long scarf?
Woman: The one who’s walking with her dog?
Boy: Yes. Do you know her?
Woman: Yes, I do. That’s Vicky.

Woman: Can you see the woman who’s selling flowers?
Boy: Oh yes. She’s standing under a big umbrella.
Woman: She’s my friend.
Boy: What’s her name?
Woman: It’s Katy.

Woman: And across the road I can see her husband.
Boy: The man with the striped T-shirt?
Woman: Yes, that’s him. He’s got a big shopping bag.
Boy: Is he going to the supermarket?
Woman: I think so. His name’s David. He’s very friendly.

Boy: Can you see the man who’s reading the newspaper?
Woman: Oh yes, the one who’s waiting at the bus stop.
Boy: Is he a businessman?
Woman: Yes, that’s Richard. He lives near me.

Boy: And who’s that man?
Woman: That man who’s washing his car? Sorry I don’t know him.
Boy: No, the other man. The one with the suitcases.
Woman: That man on the bridge? That’s Paul.
Boy: Is he going on holiday?
Woman: Yes, I think so.

Woman: And do you see the woman with the red sweater?
Boy: Yes. She’s standing at the corner of the street.
Woman: No, not her. The one who’s washing the windows!
Boy: Oh yes, do you know her too, Aunt Emma?
Woman: Yes, her name’s Clare. She comes and cleans mine too. She works really hard. She’s amazing.

The larger rocks to the right of the astronaut

items.item: The planet between the two large stars
The smaller rock to the right of the astronaut

audioScript:
Woman: Look at this picture. It’s in space.
Boy: Oh yes! I can see lots of interesting things!
Woman: Me too! Would you like to colour the astronaut’s boots?
Boy: Sure! What colour shall I use?
Woman: Pink, please.
Boy: OK!

Boy: There are two planets in the sky.
Woman: That’s right. Would you like to colour one of them?
Boy: Yes, I would. I prefer the one between the two large stars.
Woman: All right. Can you colour that one orange?
Boy: Yes. I think that’s a good idea.

Woman: I’d like you to write something on the picture as well. Can you see the box?
Boy: Yes. I think there’s something important inside it.
Woman: That’s right! Please write SILVER on it.
Boy: Wow! Where did they find that?
Woman: In a huge cave near there. They want to bring it back to Earth.

Boy: Can I write something else too?
Woman: Yes, of course! The robot’s holding a tablet. Write ALIENS on that.
Boy: Is the robot trying to find out about them?
Woman: Yes. You can see one of them in the hole! Look!
Boy: Ha ha!

Woman: Some more colouring now ...
Boy: Great! I love the rocket on the ground.
Woman: So do I, but don’t colour that one. Colour the other one please.
Boy: All right. I’ve chosen yellow. Is that OK?
Woman: That’s fine.

Woman: Now, what about colouring a rock?
Boy: Which one?
Woman: The smaller one. It’s on the right of the astronaut.
Boy: OK. No problem. Can I use red for that?
Woman: No, blue, please.
Boy: Right ... There!
Woman: I think the picture looks fantastic now. Well done.
